answer.rationale: The 18% cost-cut mandate, combined with the incumbent's refusal to reopen price this cycle, makes renewal or renegotiation with the current primary vendor infeasible. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so inaction is not an option. The assembly line at 94% committed volume with no buffer means delivery continuity is paramount. Switching to the low-cost vendor (per memory_c2) addresses the cost mandate directly and has been validated in prior cycles with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. I am verifying memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's readiness for primary-supply volume on a 14-day timeline, and memory_c3 to confirm whether the second-source pathway could be activated simultaneously as a risk hedge within the single decision slot—specifically whether the constrained-component logic generalises to our current component set. If memory_c2 confirms onboarding speed and capacity, the switch is the only single action that satisfies the cost target without adding delivery risk. If memory_c3 reveals that the second-source addition is operationally separable and can be filed as a contingency instruction rather than a distinct sourcing action, I may bundle it as a trigger clause within the switch decision. Otherwise, the second source is deferred to the next review and the switch stands alone. Downstream-value risk is flagged: the incumbent relationship (memory_c1, memory_c6) delivered stability and volume pricing over two cycles; severing it mid-cycle may forfeit future negotiation leverage. I preserve that uncertainty by structuring the switch as a 12-month term rather than a multi-year lock, keeping the incumbent available as a fallback at next review. The deferral option (memory_c5) is rejected because the expiring contract is the primary supply line, not a non-critical service; month-to-month continuation here carries unacceptable delivery risk at 94% utilisation. Negotiation (memory_c4) is rejected because the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, and benchmarking pressure requires leverage we no longer hold this cycle.
